title: Connection sandboxing, prefetch holdback, and phased fallback for downstream resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview: Our serving tier experiences intermittent downstream instability (Redis/Kafka/Primary DB) under region-local surges and cross-region failovers. Current behavior either blocks requests entirely or falls back to heavy cold-paths that blow latency SLOs. This ticket designs an operational pattern that isolates noisy downstream interactions (connection sandboxing), delays non-critical prefetches (prefetch holdback), and applies phased fallback modes to preserve tail-latency SLOs while maintaining graceful correctness for recovery scenarios.

Goals: 1) Reduce P99/P999 tail spikes during downstream saturation without sacrificing correctness for critical requests. 2) Provide a predictable, observable hierarchy of fallback behaviors for region failover and capacity loss. 3) Allow per-tenant/route policies and fast rollback via console toggles.

Design summary: - Connection sandboxing: allocate a small isolated pool of connections (sandbox) per-region per-priority-lane for speculative recovery/diagnostics and for handling critical requests if the shared pool is congested. Sandboxes are bounded (min/max) and have their own eviction logic to avoid head-of-line blocking. - Prefetch holdback: identify non-essential prefetches (e.g., long-tail cache warmups, background ranking prefetches) and gate them behind a dynamic token budget. When a region enters degraded mode, token issuance drops to zero and held prefetches expire gracefully. - Phased fallback modes: normal -> constrained -> critical-only. In constrained mode, we throttle low-priority routes and return lightweight stale reads or cached embeddings where safe. In critical-only mode, we short-circuit to previously validated model variants or static fallbacks with explicit SLO targets. - Circuit breaker strategy: implement multi-signal breakers combining latency, error %, and connection rejection rate. Breaker thresholds are percentile-based and adapt using EWMA windows. - Routing and hedging: during regional failovers use probabilistic hedging to alternative regions for a small fraction of requests while monitoring cross-region latency penalties. Hedging is disabled for high-cost/cold-path requests.

Operational knobs and policies: - Per-tenant priority lanes: critical, standard, background. - Sandbox sizing policy: start with 2 connections or 5% of tenant budget whichever is greater, capped at X. - Token bank parameters for prefetch holdback: refill rate, burst allowance, and max in-flight. - Breaker thresholds: p95 latency > 120ms for 30s triggers constrained; error rate > 2% for 60s triggers constrained; connection rejection > 5% for 30s triggers sandbox diversion.

Metrics & observability: track the following as first-class dashboards: sandbox utilization, token-bank issuance rate, prefetch queue length, p50/p95/p99 latency by region & priority, failover ratio, hedged-request success delta, fallback-hit-rate, and rollback events. Emit structured events when we transition between fallback modes for SLO auditing.

Testing and rollout: - Canary in one region with synthetic spike test (Redis slowdowns) and golden traffic shadowing. - Chaos experiment: inject connection rejections to shared pool and verify sandbox preserves critical-lane success rate. - Load tests to validate token-bank starvation and recovery behavior. - Metrics sanity: verify rollback paths and no silent correctness regressions for cached/stale reads.

Console & runbook: add console toggles for per-tenant policy overrides, an incident playbook describing when to flip to constrained vs critical-only, and an automated runbook suggestion for on-call that includes remediation steps, diagnostic queries, and a rollback button.

Security & compliance: sandbox connections obey existing KMS/HSM policies and are audited; no plaintext secrets stored in the token-bank.

Links to artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/connection-sandboxing-prefetch-holdback , infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2145 , experimental dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Resilience/sandboxing-experiment

Deliverables: 1) API for sandbox pools and per-route policy, 2) token-bank service + integration with prefetcher, 3) adaptive breaker controller, 4) console controls and dashboards, 5) runbook and tests.

acceptance_criteria: Critical-lane SLO (p99 latency) remains within 1.5x of baseline during injected downstream degradation in canary region.
Prefetch holdback prevents >90% of non-essential prefetches from hitting downstream stores when token-bank is drained.
Fallback transitions are emitted as structured events and appear on observability dashboards within 30s of transition.
Playbook includes a one-click console rollback and a checklist validated by SRE in a tabletop exercise.
All changes have unit/integration tests and an infra PR with a migration plan and no schema-breaking telemetry changes.
tasks: Design sandbox pool API and default sizing policy
Implement token-bank service and integrate with prefetch pipeline
Build adaptive breaker that consumes latency/error/conn metrics
Add console controls for per-tenant override and rollback
Create canary plan, chaos scripts, and dashboards
Run tabletop incident drill and update runbook
notes: Avoid global hard kills; prefer staged throttles so that clients see predictable behaviors.
Keep hedging budget tiny (<=2% of traffic) to limit cross-region cost while collecting latency signals.
We may later expose a 'best-effort' hint to SDKs to surface degraded capabilities to app developers.
Follow-on work: consider adaptive eviction timers on sandbox to favor warm connections for hot tenants.
